claude.result:
Perfect! All 337 tests pass. I've successfully implemented customer merging functionality:

**Added mergeCustomers(customers, invoices, fromId, intoId) to src/customers.js:**
- Returns ok({ customers, invoices }) with merged customer data
- Removes the fromId customer from the customers array
- Reassigns all invoices from fromId to intoId
- Normalizes both IDs (trim and uppercase) before processing
- Does not mutate input arrays (returns new arrays)
- Errors:
  - SAME_CUSTOMER if both IDs refer to the same customer (after normalization)
  - CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND if either customer doesn't exist in the customers array

**Added SAME_CUSTOMER error code to src/errors.js**

**Added 16 comprehensive tests covering:**
- Basic merge of two customers
- Reassigning invoices from source to target customer
- Keeping target customer's existing invoices
- Rejecting merge of same customer
- Rejecting merge with normalization edge cases
- Customer not found for source ID
- Customer not found for target ID
- Handling unnormalized IDs (spaces, lowercase)
- Input immutability (customers array)
- Input immutability (invoices array)
- Removing only source customer (keeping others)
- Multiple invoices from different customers
- Empty invoices list
- All invoices from source customer
- Preserving invoice data during merge
- Normalizing both IDs for comparison

Example usage:
```javascript
const customers = [
  { id: 'C-001', name: 'Old Company', ... },
  { id: 'C-002', name: 'New Company', ... }
];
const invoices = [
  { customerId: 'C-001', number: 'INV-001', ... },
  { customerId: 'C-001', number: 'INV-002', ... }
];

const result = mergeCustomers(customers, invoices, 'C-001', 'C-002');
// result.value.customers contains only C-002 (C-001 removed)
// result.value.invoices both have customerId: 'C-002'
```

All 337 tests passing (321 previous + 16 new customer merge tests).
